title: INT8 matmul dispatch rules + shape guardrails with baseline fallback
author: Grace Kim
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds INT8 GEMM dispatch guardrails + safe fallback to baseline kernels when unsupported (shape/alignment/arch). No behavior change unless INT8 mode enabled via existing quantization config/flags.
commits: runtime/kernels: add INT8 GEMM capability query + dispatch entry points
runtime/kernels: encode shape/alignment guardrails; fallback to fp16/bf16 baseline
runtime/tests: add INT8 matmul correctness tests (shape sweep + edge cases)
runtime/bench: annotate kernel mode + fallback reason in perf artifacts
description:
Motivation: As part of the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint (ENG-7424), we need deterministic and safe selection of the INT8 GEMM path. Prior to this PR, INT8 could be requested via quantization config, but dispatch was overly optimistic and would attempt INT8 kernels for shapes/alignments that the backend can’t handle reliably across SKUs, leading to either correctness failures (rare) or silent perf cliffs due to internal reformatting.

What this PR does: Implements explicit INT8 matmul dispatch rules, shape constraints, and a transparent fallback to baseline kernels when the INT8 path is unsupported. This is intentionally conservative; we can widen support after the benchmark matrix validates additional regimes.

Dispatch rules (high level): (1) Only consider INT8 GEMM on supported GPU arch (sm80+). (2) Require weight-only INT8 layout to be present (prepacked/registered) and runtime activation to be INT8-enabled via quantization profile. (3) Enforce shape/alignment guardrails: K must be a multiple of 32, N must be a multiple of 8, and the activation/weight pointers must be 16B-aligned (to avoid slow paths). (4) Enforce a minimum tile utilization threshold (avoid INT8 for tiny GEMMs where packing/launch overhead dominates); default threshold is (M*N) >= 4096, configurable via an internal knob for benchmarking.

Fallback behavior: If any guardrail fails, we fall back to the existing baseline GEMM (fp16/bf16 as previously selected) and record a structured fallback reason for benchmarking and later heuristics work. Fallback is non-fatal and does not change numerics relative to current behavior.

New metadata/debugging: Adds a small, structured annotation to the benchmark artifact metadata to help interpret “INT8 requested but not used” cases. This includes kernel_mode_selected={int8|baseline} and fallback_reason={arch_unsupported|shape_k|shape_n|alignment|missing_prepack|too_small}.

Correctness/testing: Adds unit tests that compare INT8 GEMM outputs against the baseline reference for a shape sweep that includes both supported and intentionally-unsupported shapes. For supported shapes, we validate within INT8 expected tolerance (and explicitly validate we don’t NaN/Inf). For unsupported shapes, tests assert that we take the fallback path and match baseline bit-for-bit (since INT8 is not executed).

Illustrative snippet (dispatch guardrails):
- can_use_int8 = (sm >= 80) && (K % 32 == 0) && (N % 8 == 0) && aligned16(activations) && aligned16(weights) && has_prepacked_int8(weights_id) && (M*N >= min_mn_threshold)
- if !can_use_int8: return baseline_gemm(fallback_reason)

Performance notes: This PR does not claim a speedup by itself; it makes benchmark runs interpretable and prevents outliers caused by accidental slow paths. Early spot checks on H100 show reduced variance when sweeping common hidden sizes because unsupported shapes no longer attempt INT8 and then internally repack.

Rollout/compatibility: No default behavior change unless INT8 mode is enabled via quantization profile/flags. The fallback path is designed to be safe for production rollout behind the existing kernel-mode gating.

Links: Linear ENG-7424 (INT8 matmul integration + correctness fallbacks), ENG-7422 (harness updates). Related PRs in the sprint: pr-19827 (FP8 attention integration behind flag), pr-19863 (kernel autoselect heuristics).
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka (review): Guardrails look good. Can we make the fallback reason visible in perf artifacts? Otherwise matrix triage will be painful when INT8 silently drops to baseline.

Grace Kim (author): Added fallback_reason + kernel_mode_selected to artifact metadata (see runtime/bench/artifacts/metadata_writer.cc) and included in JSON output. Also added a counter dimensioned by fallback_reason for internal runs (not exported to customer metrics).
Rina Kobayashi (review): The alignment requirement is correct, but please make sure we don’t hard-fail when activation pointers aren’t aligned (some callers might not guarantee it).
Grace Kim (author): Yep—alignment is a guardrail only; we fall back to baseline and record fallback_reason=alignment. Added a unit test that forces misalignment and asserts baseline is used.
Noah Patel (review): The min (M*N) threshold seems arbitrary; can we at least make it configurable for bench so we can explore? Also please add comments explaining why 4096.

Grace Kim (author): Added an internal config knob runtime.int8_gemm_min_mn (default 4096) with a comment referencing launch/packing overhead from microbench. Bench harness can override via config file/env.
Claire Dubois (review): Correctness tests: please include K%32 edge and N%8 edge cases, and verify we don’t accidentally run INT8 for those shapes.
Grace Kim (author): Added explicit test cases for (K=...+16) and (N=...+4) and assertions that fallback_reason matches shape_k/shape_n and baseline path is taken.
Hiro Tanaka (approval): Approved. This should unblock clean matrix runs for INT8 while we refine heuristics.
